## My thinking this year

I'm 73 now, 55 years on this land. My wife helps where she can, but it's just the two of us most days — the children are in town, they send money sometimes but they don't come back for harvest. That shapes everything I decide.

I have 12 mu. I'll keep 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 4 mu in cotton. I used to do more cotton — it pays better per mu if you get good fiber — but picking cotton is back-breaking work and I can't do 8 mu of it anymore. Four mu is what my wife and I can manage with maybe 10-12 days of hired help for the later picks.

For wheat, I plant Jimai 22 around October 10th — it's been reliable here, good cold tolerance, and I saved part of my seed from last year's crop, buying only a portion of certified seed to refresh. I'll put down about 12 kg N/mu as diammonium phosphate before planting, then topdress 6-7 kg N/mu as urea at jointing in late March. Soil here runs moderate P, low K — I add 5 kg P₂O₅ and 4 kg K₂O at base. This is how the extension people explained it twenty years back and my own records confirm it: the split application gives me steadier yield than dumping it all up front. I expect around 480 kg/mu if the spring stays normal — my ten-year average is 465.

Irrigation for wheat: I'll pump three times — overwintering, jointing, grain filling. Maybe a fourth if May turns dry. The meter costs me about 60 yuan per mu each round, so I watch the sky before I open the valve.

For maize, right after the combine clears the wheat in early June, I no-till drill Zhengdan 958 the same week — one week is all you get. I apply 15 kg N/mu, most of it as compound fertilizer at planting with a side-dress urea at V6-V8 if the stand looks pale. Maize usually only needs one irrigation around tasseling here if the summer rains are decent. Expect 520 kg/mu.

For cotton, I plant Lumianyan around April 20th on plastic mulch — I've used mulch since the nineties, saves water and gets the temperature up. Cotton gets less nitrogen than people think — I do 13 kg N/mu split three ways: base, first flower, peak flower. Too much N and you get all leaf, no bolls. I'll spray for aphids and bollworm as needed, usually 3-4 sprays. Expected lint: 260 kg/mu.

Total out-of-pocket looks like around 9,500 yuan. I keep 2,000 yuan in reserve — at my age I won't borrow, and something always comes up.
